name: Should I seal the cabin interior first, or do insulation work instead?

mainEntity.name: Should I seal the cabin interior first, or do insulation work instead?

acceptedAnswer.text: Interior sealing is best for visible joints, trim lines, and accessible gaps, while insulation work is better when the problem is heat loss through wall cavities, attics, or floors. If you are comparing options in Denver, the right choice is usually the one that addresses the actual source of the draft instead of only covering the symptom.
acceptedAnswer.description: Seal first when the issue is visible gaps and drafts around trim, doors, windows, or penetrations. Choose insulation when the main problem is broad heat loss through walls, ceilings, or floors rather than open cracks.
